heroHeadline: IFT-12 RETRY TONIGHT: Starship V3 Scrubbed at T-40s May 21 (Hydraulic Pin) — Window 6:30 PM EDT; Artemis II Crew Day 42
heroSubtitle: May 22: SpaceX cleared Starship IFT-12 for a retry tonight after yesterday's T-40s abort when a hydraulic pin in the Ship Quick Disconnect tower arm failed to retract — plus a water diverter problem and secondary QD issue on Ship 39. All three issues were resolved overnight. The May 22 window opens at 6:30 PM EDT (22:30 UTC) for 90 minutes. IFT-12 — the inaugural flight of Starship V3 (Block 3, Booster 19 + Ship 39) from the new Orbital Launch Pad 2 at Starbase — will be the first Starship flight in seven months and the first to carry a pressurized docking port and propellant-transfer interface hardware mandated by NASA as a precursor for Artemis III HLS qualification. Booster 19 (33 Raptor 3 engines) targets Gulf of Mexico water splashdown; Ship 39 flies a suborbital arc to Indian Ocean splashdown. Elon Musk stated on X: 'The hydraulic pin holding the tower arm in place did not retract.' The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen — are on Day 42 post-splashdown at Johnson Space Center. Orion heat shield inspection continues at KSC's Multi-Payload Processing Facility; Marshall Space Flight Center X-ray scans on track for summer 2026. Artemis III SLS core stage stacking advances in VAB High Bay 2. Artemis Accords at 67 nations. House Appropriations full committee markup (May 13) recommends $24.438B for NASA — flat with FY2026, rejecting the White House 23% cut.
